channel.title: CNS Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Cell, Nature, and Science.

item.title: Cell: Xenophagocytosis blockade enhances interspecies chimerism
item.description: Host macrophages limit interspecies chimerism via xenophagocytosis, whereby stressed donor cells expose phosphatidylserine as an “eat-me” signal. Blocking xenophagocytosis successfully enhances donor chimerism and enables efficient exogenic organogenesis.

item.title: Cell: Replaying germinal center evolution on a quantified affinity landscape
item.description: Antibody affinity maturation results from a somatic evolutionary process that takes place in the germinal center. A “parallel replay” experiment on germinal center B cells reveals the evolutionary forces that produce predictable increases in B cell affinity.

item.title: Cell: Deep-sea megafauna co-opts microbial energy metabolism genes to withstand ultra-long starvation
item.description: By acquiring an energy metabolism-related gene via ancient horizontal transfer from a bacterial symbiont, the deep-sea supergiant isopod gains the ability to reprogram its energy allocation, enabling survival under prolonged starvation.

item.title: Nature: Briefing chat: Spinosaurs with salt glands could have lived in marine environments
item.description: Nature, Published online: 05 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01831-y Nature staff discuss some of the week’s top science news.

item.title: Nature: First precise genome editing of human embryos triggers praise and alarm
item.description: Nature, Published online: 05 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01827-8 The ‘base editing’ technique that researchers used is far from ready for the clinic, but critics worry it will spur a rush to commercialization.

item.title: Science: Competition enables rapid adaptation to a warming range edge in a model plant community

Science: Global extent and drivers of tree cover loss quantified with high-resolution satellite data
Science: Home alone: Remote work, isolation, and mental health
Science: Homo cooperans: Understanding the nature of human cooperation

Science: Memory reactivation underlies experience-dependent adaptive regulation of sleep
Science: Fires reverse progress toward ozone air quality standards in the United States
Science: Confined growth of armchair MoS2 nanotubes at the 1-nm limit
Science: Stereoretentive radical-based alkyl-alkyl cross-coupling
Science: Ultralow chromium doping enables all-PbSe thermoelectric cooling
Science: Unexpected expansion and regrowth in Earth’s mangrove forests over the past four decades
Science: A stellar dynamical mass measurement of an inactive black hole at redshift 2
Science: Molecular mimicry of a pathogen virulence target by a plant immune receptor
Science: Landscape efficiency frontiers for biodiversity, climate mitigation, and net economic value
Science: Spontaneous problem-solving in bumble bees
Cell: Single-cell mapping of regulatory DNA-protein interactions
item.description: D&D-seq, a single-cell immune-tethering strategy, captures weak and transient DNA-protein interactions to enable integrated, genome-wide analysis of transcription factor binding across chromatin states.

item.title: Cell: Deep learning of functional perturbations from condensate morphology
item.description: A deep learning method quantitatively decodes nucleolar, nuclear speckle, and viral condensate morphology to reveal underlying biochemical states. Applying this framework reveals a previously unrecognized role for TOP1 in ribosome biogenesis and nucleolar organization.

item.title: Cell: Plasma signals of lung tumor promotion for molecular cancer prevention
item.description: A 14-protein plasma signature identifies individuals benefiting from anti-IL-1β-based lung cancer risk reduction and demonstrates how diverse tumor-promoting factors converge on the induction of an alveolar transitional state that underlies lung tumorigenesis.

item.title: Cell: Paleogenomes reveal the evolutionary relationship between modern and cave lions
item.description: Paleogenomic analysis of cave lions spanning >100 kya shows that extinct cave lions formed a long-diverged evolutionary lineage from modern lions, with distinct demographic histories and lineage-specific functional variation. Evidence of Late Pleistocene gene flow between cave and modern lions provides insight into the ecology and extinction dynamics of one of the Northern Hemisphere’s most influential megafaunal predators.

item.title: Nature: The size of tropical vegetation gross primary production
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10562-z The size of tropical vegetation gross primary production

item.title: Nature: A natural depsipeptide antibiotic binds the E-site of the bacterial ribosome
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10589-2 Improved fractionation strategies can identify antibiotics with previously unseen scaffolds and mechanisms, exemplified by manikomycin from Streptomyces rimosus, which acts by targeting the E-site of the bacterial large ribosomal subunit.

item.title: Nature: Earth’s east–west albedo symmetry
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10624-2 Analysis of a 25-year satellite record shows that Earth has a persistent east–west albedo symmetry split at 27° E, with clear-sky albedo, cloud radiative effect and open-ocean fraction exhibiting a triple symmetry around this meridian.

item.title: Nature: Relativistic electron acceleration at the bow shock of Jupiter and beyond
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10473-z NASA’s Juno observations show relativistic electron acceleration at the bow shock of Jupiter and establish a universal scaling law linking shock size to maximum cosmic ray energy.

item.title: Nature: Acquired genetic and cell-state changes in IDH-mutant glioma progression
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10612-6 Longitudinal transcriptomic, chromatin and genomic analyses of the two types of IDH-mutant glioma reveal in detail how disease progression is influenced by interdependent genetic, epigenetic and microenvironmental factors.

item.title: Nature: Mining triggers extensive additional deforestation in sub-Saharan Africa
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10551-2 Extensive mining activity leads to large-scale deforestation of dense tropical forests across sub-Saharan Africa, driven particularly by key energy transition minerals such as cobalt.

item.title: Nature: Cold-induced peptide signalling secures pollen resilience and crop yield
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10603-7 A small-peptide signalling axis involving RGF family members controls resilience to cold stress in tomatoes and rice; modulating this pathway prevents cold-induced yield losses.

item.title: Nature: Teosinte alleles enhance nitrogen assimilation and seed protein in maize
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10575-8 Teosinte alleles enhance nitrogen assimilation and seed protein without lowering crop yield when expressed in modern maize, providing a powerful strategy for crop improvement to meet future population demands.

item.title: Nature: Cell-type-resolved genetic variation shapes inflammatory bowel disease risk
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10627-z Single-cell mapping of cis-expression quantitative trait loci in inflammatory bowel disease revealed distal, enhancer-enriched variants detected at the cell-type level more frequently co-localize with genome-wide association study loci than those identified at the tissue level.

item.title: Nature: Plastoglobules compartmentalize nitrogen assimilation in maize
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10610-8 Chloroplast plastoglobules act as nitrogen-assimilation hubs in maize, with key enzymes enhancing nitrogen-use efficiency and offering new strategies for developing high-yield, sustainable crops.

item.title: Nature: Analysis of trade-offs of post-sorting plastic packaging
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10606-4 An analysis of post-sorting plastic packaging shows that target polymer purity is similar across source-separation and post-sorting pathways, but post-sorted plastics contain more contaminants that need to be removed before recyclate production.

item.title: Nature: Spermine is an endogenous iron chelator that inhibits ferroptosis
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10597-2 A non-canonical metabolic route for spermine synthesis mediated by ALDH18A1 limits iron availability and lipid peroxidation in hepatocellular carcinoma.

item.title: Nature: Chiral superfluorescence from perovskite superlattices at room temperature
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10637-x Chiral perovskite superlattices exhibit room-temperature circularly polarized superfluorescence, with emission intensity and polarization controllable by weak magnetic fields.

item.title: Nature: Mechanophore cross-linking enhances ballistic energy dissipation of polymers
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10557-w Embedding a small fraction of force-sensitive mechanophores as cross-links into common polymers enhances ballistic energy dissipation.

item.title: Nature: Commensal-derived acetylcholine enhances mucosal immune education
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10592-7 A diet–microbiome–host axis strengthens mucosal immune defences and reinforces host–microbiota mutualism.

item.title: Nature: Nuclear shell structure governs short-range nucleon pairing
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10616-2 The scattering of high-energy electrons from three different nuclei demonstrated that short-range-correlated pairing depends far more on the specific quantum orbitals occupied by nucleons than predicted by theoretical models.

item.title: Nature: High-pulse-energy integrated mode-locked laser using a Mamyshev oscillator
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10517-4 A Mamyshev oscillator mode-locked laser compactly integrated on a photonic-chip delivers nanojoule, femtosecond pulses.

item.title: Nature: LASER couples damage sensing to ESCRT assembly for lysosome repair
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10604-6 ATG8 conjugation on damaged lysosomes triggers rapid assembly of a protein complex containing TFG, which directs lysosomal membrane repair by recruiting ESCRT proteins to sites of damage.

item.title: Nature: Cooperation conflicts with equality when allocating public goods
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10550-3 Uniform sharing of public goods can boost cooperation in social networks, but often concentrates benefits among well-connected individuals, creating inequality despite greater collective success.

item.title: Nature: Enamel nanocrystal misorientation increased with meat-eating and agriculture
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10583-8 An analysis of enamel nanocrystal misorientation in primate and human teeth across three major dietary shifts in human evolution shows that misorientation increased with harder diets, suggesting that misorientation contributes to enamel’s resilience.

item.title: Nature: High-fidelity modular skeletons authenticate a Cambrian origin for Bryozoa
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10590-9 Exquisite early Cambrian fossils of Protomelission gatehousei and Dayingomelission hexaclitia preserve soft-tissue anatomy and skeletal microstructure, confirming that these taxa are definitively bryozoans and indicating a deeper origin for the Bryozoa than was first apparent.

item.title: Nature: Centromeric footprints preserve telomere integrity in ALT cancers
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10598-1 Centromeric DNA repeat insertions and CENP-A chromatin assembly are identified as genomic signatures that preserve telomere integrity in ALT cancer cells.

item.title: Nature: Queen cell architecture shapes honey bee queen development
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10534-3 Worker bee construction behaviour actively engineers a physicochemical niche that is crucial for queen development in honey bees.

item.title: Nature: Recovery of plastic from mixed waste boosts recycling rates but affects quality
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01759-3 Recovering plastic packaging from mixed domestic waste, as well as collecting plastic waste already sorted by households, increases recycling volumes but raises contamination and safety risks. Policies that support the sorting of plastics from mixed waste at central facilities should have strict quality standards and investment in advanced purification systems to ensure safe recycling outcomes.

item.title: Nature: White House proposes vast overhaul of US science funding: what you need to know
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01779-z The Trump administration’s proposal aims to improve transparency in federal funding, but critics fear the proposed rules would politicize research

item.title: Nature: Tiny hubs of metabolic activity optimize nitrogen use in maize
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01583-9 Structures called plastoglobules organize the enzymes that turn nitrogen into compounds needed for plant growth, offering lessons for sustainable agriculture.

item.title: Cell: Plant cell wall-plasma membrane attachments mediate stress resilience through cellulose synthase complexes and remorins
item.description: In plants, cell wall-plasma membrane attachments become evident upon severe water loss. These attachments depend on cellulose synthase complexes and remorins and mediate resilience under water stress.

item.title: Cell: Explosive cytotoxicity of ruptoblasts bridges hormone surveillance and immune defense
item.description: Ruptoblasts are a cytotoxic glandular cell type that undergoes explosive cell death, ruptosis, releasing potent, broad-spectrum agents capable of killing nearby cells. Ruptosis is triggered by the hormone and cytokine activin and driven by ER-derived calcium release amplified by the actomyosin cytoskeleton.

item.title: Nature: Global plastics treaty must be built on a foundation of monitoring
item.description: Nature, Published online: 02 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01775-3 Global plastics treaty must be built on a foundation of monitoring

item.title: Nature: Natural capital accounting needs a way to assess uncertainty
item.description: Nature, Published online: 02 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01778-0 Natural capital accounting needs a way to assess uncertainty

item.title: Nature: Is it time to ‘cap and trade’ credits for research-funding proposals?
item.description: Nature, Published online: 02 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01777-1 Is it time to ‘cap and trade’ credits for research-funding proposals?

item.title: Nature: First and last authors more likely to be men in leading science journals
item.description: Nature, Published online: 02 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01495-8 Women’s participation in science has risen sharply, but a Nature Index analysis finds that gender gaps in first and last authorship — markers of key scientific achievements — have barely shifted over the past decade.

item.title: Nature: Enantioselective hydrogen atom relay via non-covalent catalyst assembly
item.description: Nature, Published online: 01 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10692-4 Enantioselective hydrogen atom relay via non-covalent catalyst assembly

item.title: Nature: Passive heart-rate monitoring during smartphone use in everyday life
item.description: Nature, Published online: 01 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10507-6 A machine-learning model that uses smartphone cameras to measure heart rate in the background during normal daily phone use and subsequently estimate resting heart rate could make it easier for people to monitor heart health.

item.title: Cell: Physiological brain clearance architecture revealed by neuronal protein tracing
item.description: Neuronal protein tracing, unlike CSF tracers, reveals that brain clearance follows a “nearest exit” principle through distinct border immune niches disrupted differently by disease.

item.title: Cell: Decoding the spatiotemporal development of human meninges
item.description: A spatiotemporal atlas of the human meninges during early-to-mid gestation identifies asynchronous layer development and transcriptomic features of meningeal cells and demonstrates that pial fibroblasts recruit several meningeal macrophages via CXCL12-CXCR4 signaling to regulate Cajal-Retzius cell development.

item.title: Cell: Structural basis of Wnt signalosome extracellular complex assembly
item.description: Cryo-EM structures of Wnt3a/Fzd8-CRD/LRP6-E3E4 reveal assembly and activation mechanisms of the Wnt signalosome extracellular complex.

item.title: Cell: Farnesylation-driven KRAS phase separation promotes colon tumor growth
item.description: Through farnesylation-driven phase separation, KRAS forms cytoplasmic condensates that facilitate its processing and signaling, driving tumor growth and impacting G12C inhibition efficacy.

item.title: Cell: TPPP/p25 amyloid seeding activity as a specific biomarker for multiple system atrophy
item.description: Characterization of TPPP/p25 amyloid aggregation enables the development of a seed amplification assay that distinguishes MSA from related neurodegenerative diseases and serves as a CSF MSA biomarker.

item.title: Cell: Uncovering spatially resolved functional genomics with CRISPR screen sequencing
item.description: Zhang et al. present SPAC-seq, a sequencing-based spatial CRISPR screening technology capturing high-throughput perturbation libraries and spatial whole transcriptomes. Complementing this, TARDIS is developed as a statistical toolkit for spatial perturbation analysis. Together, they facilitate discoveries in spatial functional genomics, including cell localization, microenvironmental organization, pathway regulation, and ligand-receptor interactions.

item.title: Cell: Scavenger receptor class F member 2 is an intracellular receptor for hepatitis B virus
item.description: Li et al. identified SCARF2 as an intracellular receptor for HBV entry that directs internalized HBV to nuclear pore complexes and facilitates nucleocapsid release from endosomes.

item.title: Cell: Harnessing citizen science to contextualize adaptation mechanism discovery
item.description: Juxtaposing citizen science in situ observations and designed ex situ experiments through identified major genetic and environmental determinants reveals mechanisms of adaptation that shape haplotype distribution across native habitats.

item.title: Cell: Genome instability triggers intercellular DNA transfer between human cells
item.description: Mammalian cells can pass damaged pieces of their genome directly to neighboring cells via contact-dependent, nanotube-like connections. These transferred DNA fragments persist and function, revealing an unexpected route by which genome damage can propagate between cells.

item.title: Cell: Nociceptive innervation limits tertiary lymphoid structures to promote lung cancer
item.description: Nociceptive sensory neurons are engaged during lung adenocarcinoma tumorigenesis, suppressing tertiary lymphoid structure formation and blunting anti-tumor immunity. This study reveals CGRP signaling as a druggable, smoking-linked vulnerability for enhancing immunotherapy response in lung cancer preclinical models.

item.title: Cell: Cell-autonomous control of CAR signaling and receptor shedding via ADAM17-mediated proteolysis
item.description: AIR, a minimal 15-amino acid motif, enables rapid, activation-dependent shedding of surface receptors through ADAM17, allowing T cells to autonomously tune receptor expression. AIR reduces tonic CAR signaling and exhaustion, limits activation-induced cell death, enables logic-gated antigen recognition, and improves tumor clearance when engineered into CARs or endogenous receptors.

item.title: Cell: The temporal architecture of the seminiferous epithelial cycle revealed by spatial transcriptomics
item.description: Spatial transcriptomics reveals regulation of tissue timing by an intrinsic oscillator.

item.title: Cell: Transplanting light-dependent reactions for mammalian eye photosynthesis
item.description: Therapeutic delivery of LEAF, a chloroplast-derived nanoscale thylakoid supercomplex system, enables mammalian corneal cells to generate photosynthetic NADPH and ATP that suppress oxidative stress and inflammation. LEAF functions intracellularly and extracellularly to restore redox balance, establishing a light-driven therapeutic strategy with a cross-kingdom, prolonged endosymbiosis-like interaction.

item.title: Cell: Discovery and heterologous reconstitution of a plant noncanonical quasi-circadian gene regulatory network
item.description: Under low-temperature conditions that compromise the canonical circadian clock in postharvest strawberry fruits, a noncanonical circadian gene regulatory network remains functional, sustaining circadian rhythms and gating and promoting defense against gray mold.

item.title: Cell: Image-based, pooled phenotyping reveals multidimensional, disease-specific variant effects
item.description: Variant in situ sequencing (VIS-seq) links genetic variants to cell images, revealing how variants affect molecules, subcellular structures, and cells at scale. Applied to thousands of LMNA and PTEN variants, VIS-seq illuminated how variants impacted a multidimensional phenotypic continuum that is not recapitulated by any single functional readout.

item.title: Cell: D-SPIN constructs regulatory network models from scRNA-seq that reveal organizing principles of perturbation response
item.description: D-SPIN is a computational framework for constructing mechanistically interpretable, generative models of cellular regulatory networks from single-cell mRNA-seq data. The framework models how perturbations change cell states by reconfiguring the underlying regulatory interactions, revealing global organization and key regulators of perturbation responses, as well as mechanisms of combinatorial drug responses.

item.title: Cell: Galvanin (TMEM154) is an electric-field sensor for directed cell migration
item.description: Galvanin is an electric-field sensor that links electrical cues to directed migration in rapidly moving cells.

item.title: Cell: RegVelo: Gene-regulatory-informed dynamics of single cells
item.description: RegVelo introduces an end-to-end generative framework that jointly infers gene regulatory networks and developmental dynamics. It serves as an actionable in silico “cell,” enabling researchers to simulate regulatory perturbations and generate testable hypotheses about the mechanisms underlying cell fate decisions.

item.title: Cell: Multimodal clocks of human aging
item.description: A multidimensional framework established to quantify human aging reveals highly conserved aging biomarkers and trajectories across multiple centers. By decoding the asynchrony of organ decline, the study demonstrates that the accumulation of liver-derived coagulation factors acts as a mechanistic driver of vascular and systemic aging.

item.title: Cell: Ferroptosis inhibition enhances liver and lung graft function
item.description: Veeckmans et al. demonstrate that ischemia-reperfusion injury triggers an early lipid peroxidation wave in human transplants. They further show that pharmacological ferroptosis inhibition with FXT-001 suppresses lipid radical propagation, modulates iron homeostasis, and improves liver and lung graft function in porcine and human perfusion models.

item.title: Cell: AI-predicted spatial transcriptomics unlocks breast cancer biomarkers from pathology
item.description: Path2Space predicts spatial gene expression directly from histopathology, enabling low-cost, large-scale characterization of the tumor microenvironment. The inferred spatial breast cancer landscapes reveal clinically relevant subgroups and improve the prediction of treatment response from routine H&E slides alone.

item.title: Cell: Genetic basis of phytoalexin-mediated chemical defense in plants
item.description: Plants produce phytoalexins to defend against pathogens. Here, we identify the complete biosynthetic pathway of the fungicidal phytoalexin debneyol, highlighting MCD1 as a key regulator that confers broad-spectrum resistance against fungi, viruses, and bacteria.

item.title: Cell: The rise of polyploids during environmental upheaval
item.description: From the dating of 132 ancient whole-genome duplication events across 470 angiosperms, paleopolyploidization events cluster around pivotal periods of environmental upheaval and extinction, notably the Middle Miocene Disruption, the Eocene-Oligocene Transition, the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum, the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction, and different oceanic anoxic events.

item.title: Cell: A blood-brain barrier-like vascular gate limits immunotherapy efficacy in neuroendocrine cancers
item.description: A blood-brain barrier-like vascular gate in small cell lung cancer and other neuroendocrine cancers blocks immune cells and drives resistance to immunotherapy. Targeting the proteins IGF1R or IGFBP5 boosts CD8+ T cell infiltration and enhances anti-PD1 therapy.

item.title: Cell: Virological characteristics of SARS-CoV-2-related coronaviruses dynamically circulating in Southeast Asia
item.description: A study by the G2P-Asia consortium provides a comprehensive analysis spanning fieldwork, as well as experimental and computational investigations into the biology, evolution, and ecology of novel SARS-CoV-2-related coronaviruses from horseshoe bats in Southeast Asia.

item.title: Cell: Biodiversity and biogeography of the multi-kingdom cancer microbiome
item.description: A host-filtering and decontamination pipeline was benchmarked and applied to 16,369 tumor genomes, providing a high-resolution atlas of the cancer microbiome. Although most cancer types lacked a detectable microbiome, orodigestive cancers harbored complex multi-kingdom microbial communities that varied by site, subtype, and somatic mutation burden, linking the tumor microbiome to host phenotype and tumor genomic context.

item.title: Cell: Genetic variation reveals a homeotic long noncoding RNA that modulates human hematopoietic stem cells
item.description: A blood cancer-protective inherited variant in the homeotic lncRNA HOTSCRAMBL alters HOXA9 splicing, fine-tuning hematopoietic stem cell self-renewal while constraining HOXA-driven blood cancers.

item.title: Cell: An anaerobic pathogen rewires host metabolism to fuel oxidative growth in the inflamed gut
item.description: Enterotoxigenic Bacteroides fragilis (ETBF), a classically anaerobic pathogen, uses its toxin, BFT, to remodel host metabolism and generate a localized oxidative niche in the colon. By shifting epithelial cells toward fermentative metabolism, ETBF increases lactate and oxygen availability, allowing this anaerobe to deploy oxidative metabolism to adapt to and thrive in the inflamed gut.

item.title: Cell: Distinct in vivo dynamics of donor-derived stem cell memory CAR T cells post-allogeneic HSCT relapse
item.description: Donor-derived CD8⁺ CAR TSCM cells exhibit enhanced expansion and a favorable safety profile, inducing complete responses at low doses without lymphodepletion. Their distinctive in vivo behavior and differentiation trajectory establish TSCM cells as a robust and safe platform for next-generation CAR T cell therapy.

item.title: Cell: Differential inhibition of Morbillivirus and Henipavirus polymerases by ERDRP-0519 and structure-guided inhibitor optimization
item.description: ERDRP-0519, originally developed against the measles virus, cross-inhibits the Nipah virus with reduced potency. Structural insights reveal the basis of this differential inhibition and guide the design of improved inhibitors against Nipah virus.

item.title: Cell: Sensing endoplasmic reticulum redox state by ethylene receptors
item.description: Ethylene receptors function as ER redox sensors. Redox-dependent disulfide bond dynamics modulate receptor stability and activity, thereby tuning ethylene signaling for environmental adaptation. ER redox sensing may represent an ancestral receptor function that predates substantial ethylene biosynthesis.

item.title: Cell: Stabilizing MARCH7 as a ferro-guardian against ferroptosis
item.description: MARCH7 prevents ferroptosis by regulating intracellular iron release and extracellular iron uptake. A small molecule stabilizer, EmodAn, offers robust cardioprotection, highlighting MARCH7 as a promising target for treating ferroptosis-related diseases.

item.title: Cell: Global genetic interaction network of a human cell maps conserved principles and informs functional interpretation of gene co-essentiality profiles
item.description: CRISPR perturbation of ∼4 million gene pairs in human HAP1 cells maps ∼89,000 genetic interactions, revealing a hierarchical network that links genes to complexes, pathways, and cellular processes and elucidates the genes underlying cancer cell genetic dependencies.

item.title: Cell: Engineered commensals for metabolic modulation of the gut-liver-brain axis
item.description: Engineered Lactobacillus plantarum strains metabolize ammonia and reshape amino acid balance in hepatic encephalopathy. In two mouse models, treatment lowers blood and brain ammonia, improves anxiety-like behavior, and preserves gut microbiota diversity, while the engineered strains are cleared after dosing stops.

item.title: Cell: A skin-hypothalamus axis couples heat stress and metabolic dysfunction
item.description: Heat stress activates a skin-hypothalamus axis via KLK14-dependent epigenetic reprogramming of LRRC7⁺ astrocytes, thereby exacerbating diet-induced metabolic dysfunction. Vitamin A reduces KLK14 levels and mitigates metabolic impairment in both mice and humans.

item.title: Cell: The evolution of high-order genome architecture revealed from 1,000 species
item.description: Comparative Hi-C analysis across 1,025 species reveals that genome architecture has evolved along distinct trajectories, with plants favoring global folding and animals developing checkerboard compartmentalization, yet both converge on spatial organization as a conserved strategy for gene regulation.

item.title: Cell: Somatic cancer variants enriched in Alzheimer’s disease microglia-like cells drive inflammatory and proliferative states
item.description: Cancer-associated somatic variants are enriched in the brain immune cells of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) patients, driving them toward inflammation and proliferation, which may contribute to neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration during AD progression.

item.title: Cell: Systematic discovery of pro- and anti-HIV host factors in primary human CD4+ T cells
item.description: Genome-wide CRISPR activation and knockout screens in primary human CD4+ T cells systematically identify host proviral and antiviral factors modulating HIV infection, including the strongly antiviral factor PPID, which is shown to bind HIV capsid and reduce its nuclear import.

item.title: Cell: 2'3'-cGAMP-induced membrane shearing promotes broad antiphage immunity
item.description: An evolutionarily conserved CBASS transmembrane effector—ancestral to the mammalian cGAS-STING pathway—is activated by 2'3'-cGAMP to assemble into membrane-spanning filaments that disrupt membranes via a newly defined mechanism of vertical lipid shearing.

item.title: Cell: Gut microbiome is associated with recurrence-free survival in patients with resected high-risk melanoma receiving adjuvant immune checkpoint blockade
item.description: In 674 high-risk melanoma patients across five regions, the gut microbiome differs by region but remains stable during ICB treatment, and region-specific bacterial markers predict relapse.

item.title: Cell: p53 safeguards chemical reprogramming of human somatic cells toward pluripotency
item.description: In contrast to its barrier role in transcription factor-driven reprogramming, p53 is indispensable for efficient chemical reprogramming, where p53-competent cells preserve their genomic integrity to achieve pluripotency, whereas p53-deficient cells are selectively diminished.

item.title: Cell: A phytoscreen identifies a garlic compound as a deterrent of mating and egg laying in Drosophila and mosquitoes
item.description: This study provides a paradigm for how the vast chemical diversity inherent in agricultural crops can be screened to identify compounds that deter insect disease vectors and pests. Such a “phytoscreen” identifies a garlic compound that deters mating and egg laying in mosquitoes and flies.

item.title: Cell: Sulfur partitioning from cysteine controls T cell proliferation and effector function
item.description: This study pinpoints cysteine’s sulfur as a key determinant of CD8+ T cell immune function. Intracellular cysteine partitioning between glutathione and iron-sulfur metabolism is a critical metabolic decision that controls T cell proliferation and effector function.

item.title: Cell: A 3D morphogenetic blueprint for metastatic outgrowth in breast cancer
item.description: Breast cancer macrometastases expand by activating a metastatic trabecular morphogenesis (MTM) program that redeploys developmental branching to build a fractal 3D lattice of epithelial cords, a state already and selectively present in primary tumors destined to metastasize.
